name: Maashey Glacier
full: The Bolshoy Maashey glacier complex at the head of the Maashey River (a tributary of the Mazhoy → Chuya) on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range, below the range's highest point, Maashey-Bash (4173–4177 m). The approach is from the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) at km ~801–802 (the confluence of the Chuya and Mazhoy, a footbridge, the “Meny” tourist base), 13–20 km from Aktash/Chibit; below the glacier lies the bed of the former Lake Maashey (drained in 2012).
near: The village of Aktash (~13–14 km along the highway to the start of the trail, km 788 → km 801–802); the village of Chibit (km 783; tours start from Chibit's bases, with a 14 km transfer to the bridge)
elev: Glacier snout ~2280 m, top up to ~4100 m (Institute of Geography RAS); the former lake — 1984 m; the trailhead at the Chuya — 1461 m (Novosibirsk State University report 2015); the moraine pocket of the Left Maashey — 2621 m; Maashey-Bash — 4173/4177 m
short: One of the largest glaciers of the North Chuya Range under the highest peak, Maashey-Bash (4173 m); a 3–6 day hike along a cedar valley past the bed of Lake Maashey, which burst in 2012 and left a “graveyard” of dead trees.
desc: The Maashey valley is the right branch of the Mazhoy basin on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range. The catchment of the former Lake Maashey (96.1 km²) holds 27 glaciers with a total area of about 27 km² (28% glaciated); the main one is Bolshoy Maashey, about 10 km long (marshruting), descending from ~4100 to ~2280 m. The glacier is retreating fast: 3.2 m/year in 1962–1989, 7.1 m/year in 1989–2010 and about 14 m/year after 2010 (Institute of Geography RAS, “Ice and Snow”). Above it rises Maashey-Bash (4173–4177 m), the highest point of the range; the north face is a classic of Altai mountaineering. Further down the valley, at 1984 m, lay the famous Lake Maashey (1480×423 m, up to 7.5 m deep, volume 1.21 million m³), dammed by a rockfall-moraine dam in the first half of the 18th century (dendrochronology; the media wrote “about a century ago”). On 15–17 July 2012, after prolonged rains, a mudflow cut through the dam (a breach 10 m high, peak discharge 694 m³/s) and the lake drained; now a river flows in its place, and dead trees stand on the exposed bed. The trail starts at the Chuysky Trakt (km ~801–802) at a footbridge over the Chuya below its confluence with the Mazhoy (the bridge was rebuilt after the floods of 2010 and 2012, the current one dates from 2015 and is a toll bridge), goes up the Mazhoy to its confluence with the Karakabak (≈9 km), then along the Maashey valley to the former lake (≈9 km) and radially to the glacier (≈6–10 km). Nearby are the Karakabak lakes (~2300 m) and the Alyonka lakes; the valley is linked to the Shavla lakes via the Nizhne-Shavla Pass (grade 1B).
guide: Come here if you want Shavla without the crowds: the Maashey valley is noticeably quieter. Be sure to stop at the site of the former lake — in 2012 a mudflow drained it in a couple of days, and now silvery dead trees stand among the pebbles, an eerie and beautiful sight. Start the radial hike to the glacier early: the snout retreats by almost 14 metres a year, and in front of it is a moraine lake with a view of the north face of Maashey-Bash, the highest point of the range. Camp at the “Kedrovaya” (Cedar) or “Solnechnaya” (Sunny) camp spots. Combine it with a rest day at the Karakabak lakes — another 12 km with a light pack.
see: The bed of the former Lake Maashey with its dead forest (1984 m); the snout of the Bolshoy Maashey glacier and the moraine lake; the north face of Maashey-Bash (4173 m); the confluence of the Chuya and Mazhoy (the blue Mazhoy and the muddy Chuya); the Karakabak lakes (~2300 m); the Alyonka lakes.
skip: you don't have 3–6 days for a hike and a tent — you can't drive up to the glacier. If you just want to look at Maashey-Bash, the North Chuya Range viewpoint on the Kurai steppe (km 822) is enough.
diff: Moderate: from the bridge 8–9 km to the confluence with the Karakabak (+294 m to the fork, ~1844 m at the Karakabak), another ~8–9 km to the former lake (~2000 m), radially 6–10 km to the glacier (up to ~2600 m); a crossing of the Karakabak; walking days of 5–8 h. For beginners in good shape — on tours (altai-poxod, klubgidov 12+).
when: July–August (tours run in the summer season); June — high water at the crossings; September — snow is possible.
hours: An open area; the bridge over the Chuya and the parking at the tourist base are paid, in daylight (hours not found).
daytime: Head to the glacier at dawn — before the clouds and before the streams rise (glacial melt during the day).
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to km ~801–802 (after Aktash and Geyser Lake, by the Chuya hydropower plant — km 801 per vtourisme), turn off to the “Meny” tourist base/the bank of the Chuya, leave your car at the base (in 2015 — 300 ₽ for a round-trip crossing), the footbridge over the Chuya (toll, 150 ₽ in 2015), then on foot up the Mazhoy. Tours: from Chibit's bases (km 783) a 14 km transfer to the bridge (altai-poxod). From Gorno-Altaysk to the bridge ≈360 km, from Biysk ≈450 km (by the highway's kilometre markers: Biysk km 350, the bridge km ~802; Chibit — 347 km from Gorno-Altaysk per trekkingmania). The bridge at the mouth of the Maashey/Mazhoy is sometimes damaged by floods — check its condition with locals (trekkingmania).
needcar: Yes, to the bridge — a car/bus (the Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach service passes by); beyond that only on foot or with horses.
self: Yes, with hiking experience: the trail along the Mazhoy and Maashey is well worn; to the glacier and over the pass — navigation and caution; registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations.
roadtype: Paved highway up to the turnoff; a dirt road to the base; a footbridge; then a mountain trail with a crossing of the Karakabak, moraines and kurums (boulder fields) near the glacier.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → bridge ~6–6.5 h (≈360 km); bridge → confluence with the Karakabak 3–4 h (8.6 km); → the former lake another 5–6 h (8–9 km); the radial hike to the glacier 4–6 h (6–10 km round trip depending on the programme).
stay: On the route — tents (camp spots at the Karakabak, “Solnechnaya”, “Kedrovaya”). Before the start: bases in Aktash/on the Meny River — “Legenda” from 1,440 ₽, “V gorakh Altaya” (In the Altai Mountains) from 1,700 ₽, “Zelyony Kolobok” from 5,600 ₽, “Shepot Gor” (Whisper of the Mountains) from 7,200 ₽, “Krasnye Vorota” from 7,000 ₽ (101hotels 2026); Chibit bases from 2,200 ₽ (mirturbaz 2026).
net: not found (probably no signal in the valley; there is signal near the highway around Aktash)
entry: No protected-area fees were found. Paid: crossing the bridge over the Chuya — 150 ₽ (2015); parking/passage through the “Meny” tourist base — 300 ₽ round trip (2015). Current 2026 prices were not found.
transfer: The Chibit — bridge transfer of 14 km is included in tours; no market price found. A tour with transfer: 24,000–78,300 ₽ (2026).
bring: A tent and sleeping bag (about 0…+5 °C at night near the glacier), a waterproof shell, boots + shoes for crossings, poles, sunglasses, a GPS device/offline map, food for 4–6 days, cash (bridge, base), insurance with evacuation.
warn: Mudflows and outburst floods: in 2012 a mudflow destroyed the lake and the bridges — don't go into the valley during prolonged rains. Crossings of the Karakabak/Maashey; crevasses and rockfalls on the glacier — don't step onto the ice without equipment. Registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Registration of tourist groups with the Ministry of Emergency Situations is online at forms.mchs.gov.ru (processed within a day); it is not mandatory for short outings to sites by the highway, but recommended for hikes. Ticks: by 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3600 bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured. Border zone: the border zone in Kosh-Agach District covers only part of the territory: under FSB order no. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB order no. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remain in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan District) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official reply from the Border Directorate on this specific point was found). General rules: for Russian citizens in the border zone a passport is enough, a permit is only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point of the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Sailyugem National Park website; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; the office in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible.
food: A banya at the mouth of the Karakabak (arranged by tour operators, altai-poxod); on the route — trail food; in Aktash — cafes by the highway (see Geyser Lake).
reviews: No ratings found; tours: Klub Gidov (Guides' Club) — no rating; Klub Priklyucheniy (Adventure Club) — describes it as “a harder, less popular but no less interesting” route. Pros: few people, the glacier and the dead forest; cons: a long approach, river crossings.

p.sum: The start is at km ~801–802 of the Chuysky Trakt (the “Meny” tourist base, a footbridge over the Chuya), 8–9 km up the Mazhoy to the Karakabak, another 8–9 km to the bed of the former Lake Maashey, a radial hike of 6–10 km to the glacier. 3–6 days, tents, registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Tours 24,000–78,300 ₽.
